safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is redundant (zāʾida). (يطفئوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām. (بأفواههم) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يطفئوا), and (الباء) is for instrumentality. (الواو) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) wāw in both places. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يطفئوا) is in the position of an accusative direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of a verb of wanting.
The clause «يريدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يطفئوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
The clause «اللَّه متمّ ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يريدون - or of يطفئوا. The clause «لو كره الكافرون ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun in متمّ. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "even if the disbelievers dislike the light of Allah, Allah is the One who brings forth His light and makes it manifest."

* Morphology:
(متمّ) is an active participle from the quadriliteral verb أتمّ; its pattern is مفعل, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

* Rhetoric:
The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya) in the words of Allah the Exalted يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ.
It depicts their state, in their striving to nullify the truth, as the state of one who blows at the sun with his mouth to extinguish it, in mockery and derision of them, as people say: "He is extinguishing the very eye of the sun."
Some eminent scholars held that what is meant by the light of Allah is His true religion, by way of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), and likewise in the words of Allah the Exalted وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(بالهدى) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of أرسل or from its object. (اللام) is for causation. (يظهره) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (على الدين) is attached to (يظهره), the verb being given the sense of "make it prevail" (يعليه). (الواو) is a ḥāl wāw. (لو كره المشركون) is like لو كره الكافرون [Note: in the previous verse (8).].
The clause «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «يظهره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يظهره..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (أرسل); the agent of يظهر is a pronoun referring to the word of majesty (Allah).
The clause «لو كره المشركون» is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يظهره.

safi-cedvel:10-13.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (2) of this sūra.]. (هل) is an interrogative particle. (على تجارة) is attached to (أدلّ). (من عذاب) is attached to (تنجيكم).
The clause «يأيّها الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هل أدلّكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative (jawāb al-nidāʾ).
The clause «تنجيكم ... » is in the position of a genitive naʿt (adjective) of تجارة.
11- (باللَّه) is attached to (تؤمنون). (في سبيل) is attached to (تجاهدون), and likewise (بأموالكم). The demonstrative in (ذلكم) refers to faith and striving. (لكم) is attached to (خير). (كنتم) is a defective past verb (kāna) in the position of the jussive, being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «تؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or it is an explication, according to Ibn Hishām, explaining "the trade".].
The clause «تجاهدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تؤمنون.
The clause «ذلكم خير ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «كنتم تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تعلمون ... » is in the position of an accusative khabar (predicate) of كنتم. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "then believe and strive ..."
12- (يغفر) is a jussive imperfect verb, the apodosis of an implied condition. (لكم) is attached to (يغفر). (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) [Note: with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "beneath its trees"; it is also possible that the prepositional phrase is attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار.]. (مساكن) is conjoined to جنّات, and tanwīn is withheld from it because it is a plural of the form of the ultimate plurals (muntahā al-jumūʿ). (في جنّات) is attached to a second adjective of مساكن. The demonstrative in (ذلك) refers to the forgiveness and the entry into the Gardens.
The clause «يغفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined by fāʾ, i.e. "if you do it, He will forgive."
The clause «يدخلكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «ذلك الفوز ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
13- (الواو) is a conjunction. (أخرى) is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "He will give you another blessing" (يؤتكم نعمة أخرى), jussive by conjunction to (يغفر) [Note: or it is omitted on the pattern of ishtighāl, i.e. "you love another"; it is also possible that (أخرى) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is نصر من الله, or that it is conjoined to تجارة and genitive like it.]. (نصر) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي" (it), i.e. the other blessing. (من اللَّه) is attached to (نصر). (الواو) is resumptive - or a conjunction. The clause « (يؤتكم) أخرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «تحبّونها ... » is in the position of an accusative naʿt of أخرى.
The clause « (هي) نصر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «بشر المؤمنين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Benefits:
- Conjoining a declarative (khabar) onto an imperative/performative (inshāʾ), and the reverse: most scholars forbade it, among them Ibn Mālik and Ibn ʿUṣfūr, while al-Ṣaffār and a group permitted it, citing the words of Allah the Exalted:
«فَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكافِرِينَ وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ» and His words in Sūrat al-Ṣaff, in the very verse we are dealing with: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ. تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ، يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ وَمَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ، وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).
This position, namely the permissibility of conjoining a declarative onto an imperative, is supported by the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وإن شفائي عبرة مهراقة ... وهل عند رسم دارس من معوّل
(Indeed my cure is a tear that is poured out ... and is there, at a worn-out trace of a dwelling, anything to rely on?)
al-Zamakhsharī rejected [the evidence of] the two verses, of al-Baqara and al-Ṣaff, denying the permissibility of conjoining a declarative onto an imperative. He said: As for the verse of al-Baqara, the imperative is not what the conjunction relies on, so that a match would be sought for it; rather, what is meant is to conjoin the clause of the reward of the believers onto the clause of the punishment of the disbelievers, as you say: "Zayd is punished with the shackle, and give glad tidings to so-and-so of release." He also allowed it to be conjoined to اتقوا. More complete than his words in the first answer is to say: What the conjunction relies on is the clause of reward, as he mentioned, and to this it may be added: the discourse is looked at for the meaning resulting from it, as if it had been said: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds have Gardens, so give them glad tidings of that." As for the second answer, it is open to question, because it cannot be an apodosis of the condition, since the command to give glad tidings is not conditional on the disbelievers' inability to produce the like of the Qur'an. The reply is: it is known that they are not the believers, so it is as if it had been said: "If they do not do so, give glad tidings of the Gardens to others" - the meaning being: give these obstinate ones the news that they have no share in Paradise.
And he said regarding the verse of al-Ṣaff: the conjunction is onto (تؤمنون) because it has the sense of "believe" (آمنوا). It does no harm that the one addressed by (تؤمنون) is the believers and by (بشر) the Prophet, peace be upon him, nor that it be said of (تؤمنون) that it is an explication of the trade and not a request, and that (يغفر لكم) is the answer to the question, the cause being placed in the position of the effect; for difference of agents does no harm, as in our saying "Stand, and you, Zayd, sit"; and because (تؤمنون) is not necessarily an explication. Granting that, it is still possible that it is an explication while being a command, in that the meaning of the preceding discourse would be "trade a trade that will save you from a painful punishment", as (فهل أنتم منتهون) was in the sense of "desist"; or that it is an explication in meaning and not in technical form, because a command may be conveyed to give the meaning obtained from the explicative particle. One says: "Shall I direct you to the cause of your salvation? Believe in Allah", just as you say "It is that you believe in Allah." In that case the conjunction is impossible, since giving glad tidings does not enter into the meaning of the explication.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (2) of this sūra.]. (ما) is a maṣdar particle. (للحواريّين) is attached to (قال).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قال..) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We said that, like the saying of ʿĪsā" [Note: al-Zamakhsharī, in his i'rab of the noble verse, took a course that changes the meaning of the verse, i.e.: "Be helpers of Allah as the disciples were helpers of ʿĪsā when he said to them: Who are my helpers toward Allah?"].
(من) is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (أنصاري). (إلى اللَّه) is attached to a ḥāl from the first-person pronoun, i.e. "turning toward helping Allah", that is, with an omitted muḍāf. (الفاء) is resumptive. (من بني) is attached to an adjective of طائفة. The second (الفاء) is a conjunction. (على عدوّهم) is attached to (أيّدنا), the verb being given the sense of "We strengthened" (قوّينا). (الفاء) is a conjunction ...
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كونوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause « (قلنا) ذلك كقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «قال عيسى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
The clause «من أنصاري ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال الحواريّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «نحن أنصار اللَّه ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «آمنت طائفة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or the clause is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "when ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, was raised to heaven, the people split into groups, and a group believed ..."].
The clause «كفرت طائفة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آمنت طائفة.
The clause «أيّدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كفرت طائفة.
The clause «آمنوا (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أصبحوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أيّدنا....

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(للَّه) attached to a ḥāl from the relative» , (في السموات) attached to an omitted element, ṣila of the relative, and likewise (في الأرض), ṣila of the second relative (الواو) circumstantial «2» ..
Clause: «سبّح للَّه ما في السموات ... » has no grammatical position, initial.
Clause: «هو العزيز ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the divine name «3».

safi-cedvel:2-3.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed, a specific indefinite, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative (الذين) badal from أيّ, in the position of accusative - or ʿaṭf bayān of it - (لم) attached to (تقولون), and (ما) is interrogative, its alif deleted, (ما) relative [Note: or an indefinite noun described, meaning "something", its returning pronoun omitted.
(2, 3) or in the position of accusative, naʿt of (ما).] in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi, its returning pronoun omitted (لا) negative (مقتا) tamyīz, accusative (أن) a maṣdar and accusative particle (عند) accusative adverbial attached to (كبر) ...
Clause: «النداء ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «تقولون ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا تفعلون ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (ما) «2».
Clause: «كبر ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «تقولوا ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقولوا..) is in the position of nominative, fāʿil of كبر.
Clause: «لا تفعلون (the second) ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of (ما) «3».

* Rhetoric:
Hyperbole and repetition: in the saying of the Exalted كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ.
This is among the most eloquent and most rhetorically effective speech. Its meaning aims at astonishment without the form of astonishment, to magnify the matter in the hearts of the hearers, because astonishment arises only at something that departs from its like and kind. The verb was predicated of «أَنْ تَقُولُوا» and «مقتا» was put in the accusative as its specification, indicating that their saying what they do not do is pure hatred with no admixture, owing to the extent to which hatred is rooted in it. The word "hatred" (maqt) was chosen because it is the most intense and most forceful of the words for aversion; it did not stop at making the aversion great, but made it its most intense and most abominable, and "with Allah" is more forceful than that.
Beyond these four aspects there is a fifth: the repetition of «ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ», a single expression in a single speech; among the benefits of repetition are inspiring dread and magnification. Otherwise the speech was complete without it.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(في سبيله) attached to (يقاتلون), (صفّا) ḥāl from the fāʿil in (يقاتلون) ..
Clause: «إنّ اللَّه يحبّ ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «يحبّ ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of إنّ.
Clause: «يقاتلون ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «كأنّهم بنيان ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the pronoun in (صفّا).

* Morphology:
(مرصوص), a passive participle from the triliteral (رصّ); its wazn is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
The inclusion of the specific within the general: the general prohibition came first in the third verse, then immediately after this general prohibition came the saying of the Exalted إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ.
Mentioning this directly after the general prohibition is evidence that the hatred was attached to the saying of those who had promised steadfastness in fighting the unbelievers and did not fulfil it, as you say to one who has committed a particular offence:
"Do not do what attaches shame to you, and do not curse Zayd." The benefit of such an arrangement is: prohibiting one thing twice, included in the general and singled out in particular, which is better than prohibiting it in particular twice, for that is counted as mere repetition, whereas this is repetition together with the magnification and dread that generalization carries.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (لقومه) attached to (قال), (قوم) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, omitted for lightness.
And it (the yāʾ) is muḍāf ilayhi (لم) attached to (تؤذونني), and (ما) is interrogative, its alif deleted (الواو) circumstantial (قد) for certainty [Note: that is, because of the certainty of their knowledge of his message; so it is neither for reduction nor for approximation.], (إليكم) attached to (رسول).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي رسول ... ) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تعلمون.
(الفاء) resumptive (لمّا) an adverbial meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the apodosis أزاغ (الواو) resumptive (لا) negative.
Clause: «قال موسى ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «النداء ... » is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «تؤذونني ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
Clause: «تعلمون ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the fāʿil of تؤذونني.
Clause: «زاغوا ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «أزاغ اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «اللَّه لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).

* Morphology:
(أزاغ), it has an iʿlāl whose rule is like the rule of the iʿlāl in زاغ.. See verse (17) of Sūrat al-Najm.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(وإذ قال عيسى) like وإذ قال موسى «1», (ابن) badal from عيسى, nominative [Note: or ʿaṭf bayān of it, or naʿt of it.], (إليكم) attached to (رسول) (مصدّقا) ḥāl from the pronoun in رسول (لما) attached to (مصدّقا) [Note: or the lām is redundant for strengthening, and ما is in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi of the active participle (مصدقا).], (بين) accusative adverbial attached to an omitted element, ṣila of ما (من التوراة) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in the omitted ṣila (برسول) attached to (مبشّرا), (من بعدي) attached to (يأتي), (فلما جاءهم) like لمّا زاغوا «4», and the fāʿil of جاءهم is a pronoun referring to Aḥmad [Note: the pronoun may refer to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him.], (بالبيّنات) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of جاءهم.
Clause: «قال عيسى ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «النداء ... » is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّي رسول ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
Clause: «يأتي ... » is in the position of genitive, naʿt of رسول.
Clause: «اسمه احمد» is in the position of genitive, second naʿt of رسول [Note: or in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the fāʿil of يأتي - or from رسول.]
Clause: «جاءهم ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «هذا سحر ... » is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech.

* Morphology:
(أحمد), a proper noun, one of the names of the Messenger, peace be upon him, taken from al-ḥamd (praise); it is of the form of the imperfect beginning with the hamza of the first person, so it is a diptote (denied tanwīn).

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (من) an interrogative noun in the sense of denial, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (أظلم), (ممّن) attached to (أظلم) (على اللَّه) attached to (افترى), (الكذب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: or mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for the maṣdar because it meets it in meaning.], (الواو) circumstantial (إلى الإسلام) attached to (يدعى), (الواو) resumptive (لا) negative.
Clause: «من أظلم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «افترى ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (من).
Clause: «هو يدعى ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl.
Clause: «يدعى ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
Clause: «اللَّه لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).
